analysis.is_complaint_reason: The customer expressed dissatisfaction in branch. Her ex-partner is withdrawing her wages from a joint account, causing financial loss and distress, and she wants the bank to act. This meets CH-1.
analysis.summary: [PERSON_2] holds joint account [ACCOUNT_NUMBER_1] with her ex-partner [PERSON_1]. Since they separated, he has withdrawn her wages as soon as they arrive. Note_1 records withdrawals of £300-£600 every payday since August. She describes him as controlling and says she is scared of him. This indicates possible economic abuse and coercive control. She wants the joint account frozen and a sole account opened. She must not be contacted by call or letter at the home address; she can be contacted only on the safe number [PHONE_1]. The total loss is not yet calculated but is likely over £1,000. The case needs urgent safeguarding and specialist review.

timeline.event: Withdrawals of £300-£600 from the joint account every payday.
Customer attended branch to complain, asked for the joint account to be frozen and a sole account opened, and asked not to be called or written to at the home address.
Branch recorded the safe contact number and the account reference.

analysis.severity_reason: Under CH-6, the customer is vulnerable and at risk of harm because she is scared of a controlling ex-partner. Withdrawals of £300-£600 on each payday since August are likely to exceed £1,000 in total.

vulnerability.suggested_support: Refer to Vulnerable Customer Support for suspected financial abuse. Contact only on the safe number [PHONE_1], with no calls or post to the home address. Consider a named contact and help opening a sole account. Signpost domestic abuse support. Never discuss the case with [PERSON_1].

analysis.routing_reason: Suspected financial abuse by an ex-partner, combined with fear for her safety and loss of her wages, requires a VUL-4 referral (ESC-1). The disputed withdrawals by a joint holder also need Fraud & Scams input on liability and on protecting the account. This is borderline, because a joint holder may technically be authorised to withdraw.
